[IMPORTANT] Serious Vulnerability in UPnP library used by Bitcoin Core

This also affects XT.

Edit: It seems that there is an update to XT (0.11C) that fixes the problem.

To fix:

Either

  • turn off the checkbox in the GUI under Options → Network → Map port using UPNP (see above [image in link])
  • add the line upnp=0 to your bitcoin.conf file
  • add -upnp=0 to the command line options
This is correct. You can download Bitcoin XT 0.11C here: http://xtnodes.com

Prior to adding the upnp=0 line to the .conf file a few days ago, I was getting ~60 peers. Now I'm getting just 8, after several restarts over several days. What's that about?

edit: forgot to say, I'm running bitcoin-0.10.1 on Debian 8.

I'm not the best to explain, but I'll give it a try.

From the Wikipedia UPnP page:

Universal Plug and Play (UPnP) is a set of networking protocols that permits networked devices, such as personal computers, printers, Internet gateways, Wi-Fi access points and mobile devices to seamlessly discover each other's presence on the network and establish functional network services for data sharing, communications, and entertainment. UPnP is intended primarily for residential networks without enterprise-class devices.

From the alert page on bitcoin.org:

With UPnP turned off, your node will still connect to 8 other peers on the Bitcoin network to receive new blocks and transactions. However, it will not accept incomming connections from other peers unless you manually enable port forwarding on your router. If you wish to do that—it isn’t required—please follow these instructions.

So basically you have to enable port forwarding on your router (which you should do anyway), or wait until your client has a patched version out to have more than 8 peers again.

Bitcoin XT 0.11C fixes this vulnerability. It was released today.

It can now be downloaded at http://xtnodes.com
